title: MAINT
author: dreamer2664
body:
## What changed

Ledger format enforcement for the storage repo (MAINT t-20261014-83b5).

- `tools/check_pushes.py` — validates every PUSHES.md data row: exactly 6 columns (`\|` honored as escaped content), date YYYY-MM-DD, agent one lowercase token, repo names chatcode/superocr/storage/storagecode, where-cell self-locating (`@sha` | PR ref | the ledger's own `(this commit)` / `(this row)` / `(initial)` / watch-log / `no pushes` conventions), non-empty what. Every error printed with its row number; exit 1 on any.
- `tests/test_check_pushes.py` — 9 unittest cases: valid-ledger pass, per-rule fixtures, escaped-pipe handling, the deliverable's 4-column fixture failing **with the row number**, and an integration case lints the repo's real PUSHES.md.
- `.github/workflows/ledger-lint.yml` — runs the linter + its tests on every push and PR.
- **Format repair (append-only, no text content changed):** the 2026-10-15 S74 row contained a literal `plain|lex` pipe, breaking the table to 7 columns — escaped to `plain\|lex`. Caught here first, exactly the defect class this tool exists for.

**Rebuild note (honest):** an earlier revision of this branch used a sed one-liner to resolve a PUSHES.md rebase conflict and silently dropped 16 rows; it was discarded and rebuilt from origin/main (force-with-lease; old tip 3003fa3 abandoned, never merged). The final commit re-applies the linter, the grammar extension, and the escape repair cleanly.

## How verified (commands + expected results)

```bash
python3 tools/check_pushes.py          # PUSHES.md: 83 row(s) OK, exit 0
python3 tests/test_check_pushes.py     # Ran 9 tests — OK
python3 tools/check_pushes.py FIXTURE  # 4-column row: row N: 4 columns, expected 6, exit 1
```
acceptance: unmerged legacy proposal; preserved, NOT approved or merged into canonical tooling
porting_rule: Continue on storagecode only; existing board card gets the pointer. Carry authorship/provenance and obtain ordinary review before merge.
